messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue occurs in the method `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)` as seen in the code snippet from lines 2953 to 2965. The method is intended to concatenate two arrays of generic type T. It first checks if either input array is null and returns a clone of the other array if so. Then it determines the component type of the first array (array1) and creates a new array of that type to hold the combined elements from both arrays. The elements of array1 and array2 are then copied into the new array using `System.arraycopy`. 

The failure occurs when attempting to add arrays of different but related types like Integer[] and Long[] using this method. The created new array is typed with the component type of the first array (e.g., Integer), and when `System.arraycopy` tries to copy elements from the second array (e.g., Long[]) into this array, a runtime `ArrayStoreException` is thrown as Long cannot be stored in an Integer array. 

The exception is not caught or transformed into a clearer error, which leads to a confusing exception message, as the bug report describes. The bug is due to insufficient compatibility checking for the types of the two arrays before the array creation and copying step. The logic assumes that both arrays are of the same component type T, which does not hold when the arrays have different but compatible types (e.g., Number[], Integer[], Long[]).

In summary, the root cause of the bug is that the array concatenation method blindly uses the component type of the first array to allocate the result array without verifying that the second array's component type is compatible, leading to a runtime `ArrayStoreException` rather than a clearer exception like `IllegalArgumentException`.

This diagnosis directly explains the failure of the test case `testJira567` and the complaint about unclear error reporting in the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
